pr_body:
- Should be deployed with https://github.com/ppy/osu-deploy/pull/171
- Closes #18318
- Closes #24484
- Closes #23997
- Closes #10550
- Closes #10588

## Changes
- Refactors & Renames `SimpleUpdateManager` to `MobileUpdateNotifier`
- Removes `SquirrelUpdateManager`
- Implements `VelopackUpdateManager`
- Refactors internal restart logic to utilize Velopack
- Completely removes Clowd.Squirrel as a dependency
- Removes install text from update notifications
	- Velopack won't install the updates while the program is open, it'll do
it in between restarts or before starting.  Therefore the only notification text we need is `StartDownload`, `FailDownload`, etc

## TODO
- [x] Wait for upstream changes (https://github.com/velopack/velopack/issues/151) to get merged & deployed
- [x] Remove SimpleUpdateManager
- [x] Refactor UpdateManager to work with Velo
- [x] Allow downgrading
- [x] Figure out what to do with https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/9e01cf7fc23812c4d0a76b09dd78ce6b38c06028/osu.iOS/OsuGameIOS.cs#L18 and https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/f8a2b0724d77721d4fe30fe9a4d4b457efcc73e7/osu.Android/OsuGameAndroid.cs#L83

## Next up

- Adjust windows associations to work with the static executable path (do this in a separate PR)
- Figure out what to do with:
	- https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/26558
	- https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/23635
	- https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/12324

---

NOTE: I haven't tested the update logic because of the difficulty of doing that, and the fact that bugs here would really only show themselves in a production release environment. I have tested the restarting logic and it works.

Read https://github.com/ppy/osu-deploy/pull/171 for information on migration to Velopack

Just a warning that sometimes things do break if you are using different versions of the Velopack NuGet and VPK. I try to minimize this of course, but as an example I changed the default behavior of Update.exe recently from "don't restart by default, require --restart to turn on" to "restart by default and turn off with --norestart". If you were using a mismatched package version at that time, your app may not/restart as you expect. The VPK tool will emit a warning if the version is not the same but you might not catch that in CI. Just keep that in mind!
The package version has since been updated in line with `osu-deploy` FWIW.
This should close these issues also #18318 #24484 #23997 #10550 #10588

issue_context.title: Wrong GPU selected after osu!lazer update
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug:**
I need to manually add osu to the list of programs nvidia will detect in order to run osu on my dedicated gpu (I'm using an old laptop from around 2009).
After updating osu the folder where osu is located has changed because it has the version numbers in it.
Not that it's a big issue but now I have to add the new version to nvidia's list after every update :smile:

**Screenshots or videos showing encountered issue:** 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/67192919/96352594-43a95900-10bc-11eb-8cd4-24498d2522a0.png)

**osu!lazer version:** 
2020.1017.0
comments: I'm half inclined to say this shouldn't be our problem. Unless we change our deployment/update method to not use separate executables for each version I don't know what we could possibly do to convince the vendor software to use the actual graphics card instead of the integrated one.

I've resolved this by adding a custom path appdata\local\osulazer\osu!.exe
Not sure if that's okay but if it is, maybe it can be made so that nvidia driver will find that path instead.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/67192919/96353367-1c09bf00-10c3-11eb-9a70-024c7ed6755d.png)
Sorry about that, adding just that path did not work after all.
This overlaps with / is a dupe of #5582.

I wouldn't say this is a dupe really. Also the linked issue needs discussion anyway - I'm not convinced we should be using the dGPU by default anyway - it can, depending on the system and optimisation of the game, actually result in lower frametime/higher latency (see: osu!stable).

I'll keep this open to track the issue of driver configs not persisting across updates, as this is definitely something we'll want to fix regardless.

Maybe something to consider at the point of moving away from Squirrel (if ever).
maybe try right clicking on the .exe file and selecting the GPU from there?
That is the intended way to use Windows. There's even a GPU setting somewhere in the system settings these days made for this purpose and intended to replace the NVIDIA control panel setting.

It seems a [similar method](https://github.com/velopack/velopack/blob/933b2ab9804652deeacb12a048e4f4da9ff3b1e8/src/lib-csharp/VelopackRuntimeInfo.cs#L160-L172) is used for unit test detection, but in some basic testing I couldn't break it in the same way we broke it last time (ie. inserting a `Logger.Log` call before the setup call).

"needs to be run before anything else" sounds like a common sense thing, but is there an actual reason you found which makes this a requirement? If so, I'd probably want that explicitly mentioned.

The Velopack docs suggest that you [*must*](https://arc.net/l/quote/urfqwedh) run it before everything else. However, as you found, that's not necessarily a strict requirement. In another example on Velopack's docs, code is [executed](https://arc.net/l/quote/chgyexjh) before the `.Run()`

As for me, I decided "So you should put `setupVelopack()` before everything else, but putting stuff before it isn't the end of the world as it would've been with Squirrel. So I'll tone it down a bit, and just keep the advisory since it's good practice to run it ASAP."

Though, @caesay would likely know best about this
